description: Measures blood sugar level after an overnight fast (8-12 hours). Key marker for prediabetes and diabetes mellitus.
Glycated hemoglobin indicating average blood sugar control over the past 2 to 3 months.
Iron-rich protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen from the lungs to tissues throughout the body.
Total leukocytes defending against bacterial, viral, and inflammatory infections.
Total circulating erythrocytes carrying oxygen throughout the circulatory system.
Thrombocytes critical for normal blood clotting and vascular repair.
Essential hormone precursor regulating calcium absorption, bone density, and immune response.
Cobalamin vital for neurological function, red blood cell synthesis, and cellular metabolism.
Primary cellular storage protein reflecting total systemic iron reserves.
Overall lipid measurement including low-density and high-density lipoproteins.
Low-density lipoprotein commonly termed 'bad' cholesterol associated with atherogenic plaque.
High-density lipoprotein ('good' cholesterol) scavenging cholesterol back to the liver.
Circulating dietary blood fats stored in adipose tissue, linked to metabolic and vascular risk.
Waste byproduct of muscle metabolism filtered by the kidneys; primary marker of renal filtration.
Urea nitrogen cleared by glomerular filtration; reflects renal function and hydration balance.
End product of purine nucleotide degradation; elevated in hyperuricemia and acute gouty arthritis.
Aspartate aminotransferase enzyme found in hepatic and myocardial tissues.
Alanine aminotransferase enzyme primarily concentrated in hepatocytes; key marker for liver inflammation.
Pituitary hormone stimulating thyroid thyroxine production; elevated in primary hypothyroidism.
Major extracellular cation regulating osmotic pressure, fluid homeostasis, and neuromuscular conduction.
Critical intracellular electrolyte regulating cardiac rhythm, membrane potential, and muscle contraction.
